create.name: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
create.bio:
Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a Tibetan Buddhist meditation master, born in Nepal in 1975, who leads the Tergar Meditation Community, a network of groups and centres in more than thirty countries. He first learnt to meditate as a boy under his father, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. As a child and teenager he lived with severe anxiety and panic, and it was through meditation that he found his way through it, an experience he talks about openly with students. Meeting the scientists who came to see his father sparked a lasting interest in research, and he later took part in studies of meditation and the brain with Richard Davidson, Antoine Lutz and colleagues at the University of Wisconsin.

His teaching blends traditional practice with modern findings about the mind, and it runs along two paths: Joy of Living, a set of simple meditations open to people of any faith, and the Path of Liberation, a graded training in Mahamudra and Dzogchen. Among his books are The Joy of Living and Joyful Wisdom; a later one, In Love with the World, tells of the years he spent as a wandering yogi in India after quietly leaving his monastery. His home is Tergar Osel Ling Monastery in Kathmandu, and each year he teaches retreats and workshops in person and online.

books.title: In Love with the World: A Monk's Journey Through the Bardos of Living and Dying
books.author: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche with Helen Tworkov
books.description: His own story of slipping away from his monastery to live as a wandering yogi in India, of the near-death experience that came early in that journey, and of what the experience taught him about living and dying.

books.title: A World of Difference
books.author: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
books.description: His newest book, a down-to-earth guide to finding steadiness inside ourselves when the world feels uncertain, built around inner refuge, awareness, compassion and wisdom.

courses.title: Finding Freedom in Life's Transitions: The Teachings on the Six Bardos
courses.description: An online weekend of teachings from Mingyur Rinpoche on the six bardos, the transitional states of living and dying, streamed live from Kathmandu.

free_resources.title: Beyond Mindfulness Webinar
free_resources.description: A free recorded webinar in which Mingyur Rinpoche shows how meditation can turn stressful situations and strong emotions into support for awareness. Free registration gives immediate access.
